Shipbuilding]]}} | module = | website = {{URL|http://www.larsentoubro.com/}} | footnotes = }} '''Larsen & Toubro Limited''' ('''L&T''') is an Indian multinational [[Conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]] headquartered in [[Mumbai]]. It operates in sectors including [[industrial technology]], [[heavy industry]], [[engineering]], [[construction]], [[manufacturing]], [[Electric power industry|power]], [[information technology]], [[Arms industry|defence]], and [[financial services]]. L&T was founded in 1938 in [[Mumbai|Bombay]] by Danish engineers [[Henning Holck-Larsen]] and [[Søren Kristian Toubro]].{{cite journal|last1=Shah|first1=Shashank|date=18 February 2014|title=Stakeholders Management in the Indian Construction Industry: Insights into the Approach at Larsen & Toubro's Construction Division|url=http://scholar.valpo.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1095&context=jvbl|journal=Journal of Values Based Leadership|volume=7|issue=1|access-date=11 June 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140523040114/http://scholar.valpo.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1095&context=jvbl|archive-date=23 May 2014|url-status=live}}{{Cite web |title=Larsen & Toubro (L&T) {{!}} Who we are |url=https://www.lntecc.com/who-we-are/ |access-date=2024-01-16 |website=L&T Construction |language=en}} As of 31 March 2022, the L&T Group consisted of 93 subsidiaries, 5 associate companies, 27 joint ventures, and 35 joint operations.{{Cite web |title=Check out the larsen toubro ltd Management Discussions {{!}} Live stock/Share Prices at indiainfoline.com |url=https://indiainfoline.com/company/larsen-toubro-ltd/management-discussions/348 |access-date=2023-04-01 |website=indiainfoline.com |language=en}} As of 1 October 2023, [[S N Subrahmanyan]] serves as the chairman and managing director of L&T, having succeeded [[A. M. Naik|A M Naik]].{{Cite web|date=11 May 2023|title=SN Subrahmanyan named L&T CMD, AM Naik steps down|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/company/corporate-trends/sn-subrahmanyan-named-lt-cmd-am-naik-steps-down/articleshow/100142919.cms|access-date=1 December 2023|website=The Economic Times|language=en}} {{Multiple image|perrow = 2|total_width=375|align=right |image1 = EXCON 2025, Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (880).jpg |width1 = 125px |image2 = EXCON 2025, Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (862).jpg |width2 = 125px |footer = Larsen & Toubro at [[EXCON]] 2025, [[Bangalore International Exhibition Centre|BIEC]] }} ==History== {{multiple image | direction = vertical | align = right | width = | image1 = Lotus Temple-Panoroma-Visit During WCI 2016- IMG 6471.jpg | image2 = Statue of Unity358.jpg | image3 = Narendra Modi Stadium view from the gallery.jpg | image4 = Pran Pratishtha ceremony of Shree Ram Janmaboomi Temple in Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh on January 22, 2024.jpg | footer = L&T's notable construction projects | total_width = | alt1 = | caption1 = [[Lotus Temple]], [[Delhi]] | caption2 = [[Statue of Unity]], [[Kevadia]] | caption3 = [[Narendra Modi Stadium]], [[Ahmedabad]] | caption4 = [[Ram Mandir]], [[Ayodhya]] }} Henning Holck-Larsen and Søren Kristian Toubro were in India to represent the interests of the Danish dairy equipment manufacturer [[FLSmidth]] when they founded L&T through an oral agreement in 1938. The company was legally incorporated in 1946. The start of [[Second World War|World War II]] in 1939 and the resulting blockade of trade, led Larsen and Toubro to undertake jobs and provide service facilities. The [[German invasion of Denmark (1940)|German invasion of Denmark]] in April 1940 stopped supplies of Danish products. The war-time need to repair, refit, and degauss ships offered L&T an opportunity, and led to the formation of a new company, Hilda Ltd, to handle these operations. L&T also started to repair and fabricate ships. The [[internment]] of German engineers in India who were to construct a [[soda ash]] plant for the [[Tata Group]] gave L&T a chance to enter the field of installation.{{cite web |url= http://www.larsentoubro.com/lntcorporate/LnT_Offerings/Service_Template1.aspx?res=P_ENC_COFF_SBU_SERV&srid=125&sbu=31 |title= Larsen & Toubro – Hydrocarbon Upstream |access-date= 21 June 2012 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20130507204336/http://www.larsentoubro.com/lntcorporate/LnT_Offerings/Service_Template1.aspx?res=P_ENC_COFF_SBU_SERV&srid=125&sbu=31 |archive-date= 7 May 2013 |url-status= dead }} In 1946, they incorporated Engineering Construction & Contracts Ltd. (ECC) to focus on construction projects. ECC now exists as the construction division of L&T. By 1947, the company represented the manufacturers of equipment used to manufacture products such as [[hydrogenated oil]]s, [[biscuit]]s, soaps and glass. In 1947, the company signed an agreement with [[Caterpillar Inc.|Caterpillar Tractor Company]] to market [[Heavy equipment|earth moving equipment]]. At the end of the war, large numbers of war-surplus Caterpillar equipment were available at attractive prices, but the finances required were beyond the capacity of the partners. This prompted them to raise additional equity capital, and on 7 February 1946, Larsen & Toubro Private Limited was incorporated. In 1947, the firm set up offices in [[Kolkata|Calcutta]] and [[Chennai|Madras]] and [[New Delhi]]. In 1948, {{convert|55|acre|ha|order=flip}} of undeveloped marsh and jungle was acquired in [[Powai]], Mumbai. In December 1950, L&T became a public company with a paid-up capital of {{INRConvert|20|l|year=1950}}. The sales turnover in that year was {{INRConvert|1.09|c|year=1950}}. In 1956, a major part of the company's Bombay office moved to ICI House in [[Ballard Estate]], which would later be purchased by the company and renamed as L&T House, its present headquarters. During the 1960s, ventures included the [[Utkal Machinery Limited]] (UTMAL, set up in 1960), [[Audco India Limited]] (1961), [[Eutectic Welding Alloys]] (1962) and [[Tractor Engineers Limited]] (TENGL, 1963). In 1965, the firm had been chosen as a partner for building [[nuclear reactor]]s. Dr. [[Homi J. Bhabha|Homi Bhabha]], chairman of the [[Atomic Energy Commission of India|Atomic Energy Commission]] had approached L&T in the 1950s to fabricate critical components for nuclear reactors. During the 1970s, L&T was contracted to work with [[Indian Space Research Organisation]] (ISRO). Chairman [[Vikram Sarabhai]] chose L&T as manufacturing partner.{{Cite book|last=Merchant, Minhaz|title=The nationalist : how A.M. Naik overcame great odds to transform Larsen & Toubro into a global powerhouse|year=2017|isbn=978-93-5277-288-9|location=Noida, Uttar Pradesh, India|pages=54|oclc=1021061261}} In 1976, ECC bid for a large airport [[Abu Dhabi International Airport|project]] in [[Abu Dhabi]]. ECC's balance sheet, however, did not meet the bid's financial qualification requirement. So it was merged into L&T. ECC was eventually rechristened L&T Construction and now accounts for the largest slice of the group's annual revenue.{{Cite book|last=Merchant, Minhaz|title=The nationalist : how A.M. Naik overcame great odds to transform Larsen & Toubro into a global powerhouse|year=2017|isbn=978-93-5277-288-9|location=Noida, Uttar Pradesh, India|pages=53, 55|oclc=1021061261}} In 1985, L&T entered into a partnership with the [[Defence Research and Development Organisation]] (DRDO). L&T was not yet allowed by the government to manufacture defence equipment but was permitted to participate in design and development programmes with DRDO. After the design and development was done, the firm had to hand over all the drawings to DRDO. The [[Government of India|Indian government]] would then assign the production work to a public sector defence unit or ordnance factory for manufacture. The firm currently makes a range of weapon and missile systems, command and control systems, engineering systems, and submarines through DRDO. Larsen & Toubro established a [[financial services]] subsidiary called L&T Finance in November 1994.{{cite web|url=http://www.ltfinance.com/overview.aspx|title=Overview|publisher=Larsen&Toubro|access-date=10 August 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110826063755/http://www.ltfinance.com/overview.aspx|archive-date=26 August 2011|url-status=live}} In 2015, the company began developing commercial, retail and office space around the [[Hyderabad Metro Rail]] project.{{cite web |author=V. Rishi Kumar |title=L&T Hyderabad Metro wins infrastructure award |url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/news/national/lt-hyderabad-metro-wins-infrastructureaward/article7625261.ece |work=The Hindu Business Line |date=7 September 2015}} In June 2019, the company acquired a controlling stake in IT services company [[Mindtree]].{{cite news|date=26 June 2019|title=Mindtree erases gains to settle in the red|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/mindtree-jumps-as-lt-hikes-stake-to-51/articleshow/69953716.cms|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190626104519/https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/mindtree-jumps-as-lt-hikes-stake-to-51/articleshow/69953716.cms|archive-date=26 June 2019|access-date=26 June 2019|newspaper=The Economic Times}} In 2022, L&T purchased the whole ownership stake that was held by [[Chiyoda Corporation]], a Japanese engineering company, in their joint venture, L&T-Chiyoda, which was formed in 1994.{{Cite web |date=22 November 2022 |title=Larsen and Toubro buys out partners stake in three-decade old joint venture for Rs 75 crore |url=https://www.cnbctv18.com/market/stocks/lt-joint-venture-chiyoda-stake-75-crore-epc-business-15226881.htm |access-date=13 May 2025 |website=CNBC TV18 |language=}} As of 2024, L&T is India's largest private-sector defence manufacturing company by revenue.{{Cite web |last=Bhattacharjee |first=Nivedita |date=7 March 2025 |title=L&T bets on space exploration as India expands private rocket and satellite industry |url=https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/lt-bets-space-exploration-india-expands-private-rocket-satellite-industry-2025-03-05/ |access-date=24 March 2025 |website=Reuters}} The company is also in the process of expanding its [[Space industry|space]] business, which includes manufacturing space [[launch vehicle]]s and [[satellite]]s, as of 2024. several businesses. These include: === Cement === L&T sold its 16.5 million tonne/per year capacity cement division to [[UltraTech Cement]] and also divested its 8.5% stake in A V Birla group company [[Grasim Industries]] in 2004.{{Cite web|date=14 May 2004|title=L&T cement business demerger comes into effect|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/LT-cement-business-demerger-comes-into-effect/articleshow/675137.cms|access-date=14 July 2020|website=The Times of India|language=en}} === L&T-John Deere === In 1992, L&T established a 50-50 joint venture with [[John Deere]] to manufacture tractors in India, called L&T - John Deere. L&T sold their interest to John Deere in 2005.{{cite web|title=L&T India - Error Page|url=http://www.larsentoubro.com/lntcorporate/LnT_PRS/news_news_press.aspx?res=P_CORP_EMID_BPRS&PR_ID=150|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180319004246/http://www.larsentoubro.com/lntcorporate/LnT_PRS/news_news_press.aspx?res=P_CORP_EMID_BPRS&PR_ID=150|archive-date=19 March 2018|access-date=15 June 2017|website=www.larsentoubro.com}} === L&T Case === In 1992, L&T established L&T-Case Construction with CNH Global as a 50-50 joint venture to build backhoes. In 2011, L&T sold its share to CNH, and the company was renamed Case New Holland Construction Equipment India.{{Cite news|title=L&T divests stake in L&T-Case JV|url=https://www.constructionweekonline.in/lt-divests-stake-in-lt-case-jv|access-date=14 July 2020|newspaper=Construction Week India|date=31 March 2011 |language=en}} === L&T Medical Equipment and Systems === In 1987, L&T launched the L&T Medical Equipment & Systems division.{{Cite web|title=L&T to sell medical equipment biz|url=https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/lampt-to-sell-medical-equipment-biz/article20530051.ece1|access-date=10 July 2020|website=@businessline|date=16 November 2012 |language=en}} In November 2012, it was sold to Skanray Technologies Pvt Ltd.{{Cite web|date=17 November 2012|title=L&T sells medical equipment biz to Skanray Healthcare|url=https://www.financialexpress.com/archive/lt-sells-medical-equipment-biz-to-skanray-healthcare/1032279/|access-date=10 July 2020|website=The Financial Express|language=en-US}} It manufactures surgical robots, MRI, X-ray, DR Imaging etc. === EWAC Alloys Limited === EWAC Alloys Limited was a wholly owned subsidiary of L&T. The company was engaged in design & development, manufacture and supply of special welding electrodes, gas [[brazing]] rods and fluxes, [[welding torch]]es and accessories, atomised metal powder alloys, flux cored continuous wires & wire feeders, polymer compounds & wear-resistant plates. Prof Wasserman, founder of Eutectic Castolin, and Henning Hock Larsen, founder of L&T, founded the Eutectic Division in India in the year 1962. Eutectic Castolin was later merged into the [[Messer Group]] of companies, Germany and referred as Messer Eutectic Castolin (MEC). In 2010, L&T, bought the entire stake from Messer to become the wholly owned subsidiary of it. The current headquarters is in Ankleshwar, Gujarat (India), and the products are sold under the name EWAC. L&T sold its entire stake in unlisted subsidiary EWAC Alloys to UK-registered ESAB Holdings for a total consideration of Rs 522 crore. The share purchase agreement has been executed on 11 October 2017.{{Cite web|date=12 October 2017|title=Larsen and Toubro sells EWAC Alloys for Rs 522 cr to UK's ESAB|url=https://www.financialexpress.com/industry/larsen-and-toubro-sells-ewac-alloys-for-rs-522-cr-to-uks-esab/891102/|access-date=10 July 2020|website=The Financial Express|language=en-US}} The acquirer ESAB offers products for welding and cutting process. In 2012, ESAB was acquired by Colfax Corp., a diversified industrial manufacturing company based in the US. === Petroleum Dispensing Pump (PDP) === In November 2009, Larsen and Toubro (L&T) sold its [[Gasoline pump|petroleum dispensing pump]] (PDP) business to [[Gilbarco Veeder-Root]], a US-based payments systems company, for around Rs 150 crore. Gilbarco has signed a definitive purchase agreement to acquire the business. With the completion of acquisition, L&T's PDP business will become part of a new division called Gilbarco Veeder-Root India Pvt Ltd.{{cite web | url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/l-t-sells-fuel-dispenser-biz-to-us-firm-for-rs-150-crore-109111800095_1.html | title=L&T sells fuel dispenser biz to US firm for Rs 150 crore }} === L&T Kobelco Machinery Private Limited === This was a [[joint venture]] of L&T and Kobe Steel of Japan, to manufacture internal mixers and twin screw roller-head extruder's for the tyre industry. L&T sold its entire 51% stake in L&T Kobelco Machinery Private to its joint venture partner in the company, Kobe Steel of Japan, for Rs 43.5 crore.{{Cite news|last=Prasad|first=Rachita|title=L&T sells 51% stake in JV to partner Kobe Steel for Rs 43.5 crore - The Economic Times|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/lt-sells-51-stake-in-jv-to-partner-kobe-steel-for-rs-43-5-crore/articleshow/68705621.cms|access-date=15 July 2020}} === L&T Electrical and Automation Ltd. === L&T was an international manufacturer of electrical and electronic products and systems. The company manufactured custom-engineered switchboards for industrial sectors like power, refineries, petrochemicals and cement.{{cite web|title=Larsen & Toubro Limited |url=http://www.rina.org.uk/page666.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717045722/http://www.rina.org.uk/page666.html|archive-date=17 July 2011|access-date=16 July 2010|publisher=Rina.org.u}} In the electronic segment, L&T offered a range of [[Electricity meter|metre]]s and provides control automation systems for industries. In May 2018, the firm signed a definitive agreement with [[Schneider Electric]] for the strategic divestment of its electrical and automation (E&A) business in an all-cash deal of ₹14,000 crore.{{Cite news|title=L&T to divest automation division in Rs 14,000 crore deal - The Economic Times|work=The Economic Times|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks/news/lt-to-divest-automation-division-in-rs-14000-crore-deal/articleshow/63986428.cms?from=mdr|access-date=14 July 2020}} The deal was completed on 31 August 2020 after receiving the requisite regulatory approvals. L&T has said that its exit from the electrical and automation business is a part of its strategic portfolio review process.{{Cite web|last=Thomas|first=Tanya|date=31 August 2020|title=L&T sells electrical, automation business to Schneider Electric for ₹14,000 cr|url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/l-t-sells-its-electrical-and-automation-business-to-schneider-electric-for-rs-14-000-crore-11598877278444.html|access-date=8 September 2020|website=mint|language=en}} === L&T Mutual Fund === L&T Mutual Fund was the [[mutual fund]] company of the L&T Group. Its average [[assets under management]] (AUM) as of May 2019 is {{Indian Rupee}} 73,936.68 crore.{{cite web |title=Average AUM |url=http://www.amfiindia.com/research-information/aum-data/average-aum |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131213060208/http://www.amfiindia.com/research-information/aum-data/average-aum |archive-date=13 December 2013 |access-date=8 December 2013 |publisher=Association of Mutual Funds in India}} On November 26, 2022, L&T Mutual Fund was sold to [[HSBC]].{{Cite web |title=Will L&T Mutual Fund's acquisition inject fresh life into HSBC India MF? Its co-CEO weighs in |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/personal-finance/will-lt-mutual-funds-acquisition-inject-life-in-a-comatose-hsbc-india-mf-9837831.html |access-date=2023-04-27 |website=Moneycontrol |date=10 January 2023 |language=en}} === L&T Infrastructure Development Projects Limited === Larsen & Toubro, signed an agreement to divest its stake in L&T IDPL to a portfolio company of Infrastructure Yield Plus II, an infrastructure fund managed by Edelweiss Alternatives in December 2022. The transaction is subject to completion of customary closing conditions including receipt of applicable regulatory and other approvals.{{Cite web |date=2022-12-19 |title=Larsen & Toubro divests entire 51% stake in L&T Infrastructure Development Projects |url=https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/corporate/story/larsen-toubro-divests-entire-51-stake-in-lt-infrastructure-development-projects-356873-2022-12-19 |access-date=2023-04-27 |website=Business Today |language=en}} ==Listing and shareholding== The [[equity shares]] of the company are listed on the [[Bombay Stock Exchange]] (BSE) and the [[National Stock Exchange of India]] (NSE). The company's shares constitute a part of the [[BSE SENSEX]] of the BSE as well as the [[NIFTY 50]] index of the NSE.{{cite web |url=http://www.bseindia.com/bseplus/AnnualReport/500510/5005100313.pdf |title=Annual Report 2012-13 |publisher=L&T |access-date=3 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131209055027/http://www.bseindia.com/bseplus/AnnualReport/500510/5005100313.pdf |archive-date=9 December 2013 |url-status=live }} Its [[global depository receipt]]s (GDR) are listed on the [[Luxembourg Stock Exchange]] and [[London Stock Exchange]]. === Shareholders === Shareholders as of 31 December 2022{{Cite web |title=L&T India {{!}} Downloads {{!}} Shareholding Pattern |url=https://investors.larsentoubro.com/Shareholding-Pattern-Archives.aspx |access-date=2023-04-05 |website=investors.larsentoubro.com}} {| class="wikitable" ! |website=ANI News |language=en}} == Controversy == {{Multiple issues|section=yes|{{Importance section|date=March 2025}} {{Essay-like|section|date=March 2025}}}} In January 2025, an undated video of Subrahmanyan's New Year address sparked widespread controversy online. In the video, an employee is heard asking why Larsen & Toubro, one of India's largest conglomerates, requires employees to work on Saturdays. In response, Subrahmanyan expressed remorse not being able to make employees work on Sundays, stating it would make him happier since he himself works on Sundays.{{Cite news |last=PTI |date=2025-01-09 |title='How long can you stare at wife?': L&T chairman Subrahmanyan suggests 90-hour work week |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/how-long-can-you-stare-at-wife-lt-chairman-subrahmanyan-suggests-90-hour-work-week/article69082012.ece |access-date=2025-01-10 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}} He further questioned that what do employees do "sitting at home" and how long could spouses stare at each other, suggesting that employees should "Get to the office and start working" on Sundays instead.{{Cite web |title="What Do You Do Sitting At Home": L&T Chairman Suggests Working Sundays |url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/l-t-chairman-sn-subrahmanyans-90-hours-work-a-week-statement-draws-criticism-7433804 |access-date=2025-01-10 |website=www.ndtv.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Anupam Mittal's Humorous Take On L&T Chief's 'Stare at Wife' Remark: "But Sir, If..." |url=https://www.ndtv.com/feature/anupam-mittals-humorous-take-on-l-t-chiefs-stare-at-wife-remark-but-sir-if-7455707 |access-date=2025-01-12 |website=www.ndtv.com |language=en}} Shortly after the video went [[Viral video|viral]], Meena Subrahmanyan, his wife, became the target of widespread [[trolling]] on social media due to her husband's remarks.{{Cite web |title=Meena Subrahmanyan, Wife Of L&T Chief SN Subrahmanyan, Gets The Heat From Netizens For Latter's 90-Hour Workweek Remark |url=https://www.freepressjournal.in/business/meena-subrahmanyan-wife-of-lt-chief-sn-subrahmanyan-gets-the-heat-from-netizens-for-latters-90-hour-workweek-remark |access-date=10 January 2025 |language=en-US}} Subrahmanyan justified this stance by citing a conversation with a Chinese individual who claimed that China's longer work hours could enable them to surpass the United States. He subsequently endorsed a 90-hour workweek for employees, adding that such effort was necessary for achieving success. However, his statements were contradicted by a 2021 [[United Nations]] report, which highlighted the detrimental effects of excessive work hours on mental and physical health.{{Cite news |last=Panwar |first=Sanya |date=Jan 10, 2025 |title=L&T chairman SN Subrahmanyan endorses '90-hour work week' but a UN report warns long working hours can kill you |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/lifestyle/health/lt-chairman-sn-subrahmanyan-under-fire-90-hour-work-week-reaction-un-report-long-working-hours-can-kill-you-warning-101736488457967.html |work=[[Hindustan Times]]}} The remarks reignited concerns about toxic work environments in India, especially following the 2024 suicide of an Indian Chartered Accountant and death due to heart attack of another one attributed to work pressure.{{Cite web |title=Anna Sebastian Perayil: Death of Indian employee sparks debate on 'toxic work culture' |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c0kjgp4jr5yo |access-date=2025-01-10 |website=www.bbc.com |date=24 September 2024 |language=en-GB}} This controversy also brought attention to Subrahmanyan's substantial remuneration in 2024, which amounted to ₹510,000,000 (approximately $6,000,000 in 2025), compared to L&T's median employee salary of ₹955,000 (approximately $11,000 in 2025).{{Cite web |last=Service |first=Express News |date=2024-06-11 |title=L&T CMD got Rs 51 crore salary in FY24, up 43% |url=https://www.newindianexpress.com/business/2024/Jun/11/lt-cmd-got-rs-51-crore-salary-in-fy24-up-43 |access-date=2025-01-10 |website=The New Indian Express |language=en}} Prominent figures such as [[Harsh Goenka]], [[Deepika Padukone]], [[Anand Mahindra]], [[Anupam Mittal]] and [[Cyrus S. Poonawalla|Cyrus Poonawalla]] expressed their disapproval of Subrahmanyan's remarks on social media.{{Cite web |title='She Loves Staring At Me On Sundays': Adar Poonawalla Espouses Anand Mahindra, Takes A Swipe L&T Chairman SN Subrahmanyan In The 90-Hour Debate |url=https://www.freepressjournal.in/business/she-loves-staring-at-me-on-sundays-adar-poonawalla-espouses-anand-mahindra-takes-a-swipe-lt-chairman-sn-subrahmanyan-in-the-90-hour-debate |access-date=2025-01-12 |website=Free Press Journal |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2025-01-11 |title=Love staring at my wife: Anand Mahindra's cheeky reply to 90-hour work week debate |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/trending/trending-in-india/rename-sunday-to-sun-duty-harsh-goenka-slam-larsen-and-toubro-chairman-90-hour-workweek-remark-9770894/ |access-date=2025-01-10 Larsen & Toubro Limited (L&T) is an Indian multinational conglomerate headquartered in Mumbai. It operates in sectors including industrial technology, heavy industry, engineering, construction, manufacturing, power, information technology, defence, and financial services.
L&T was founded in 1938 in Bombay by Danish engineers Henning Holck-Larsen and Søren Kristian Toubro. As of  31 March 2022, the L&T Group consisted of 93 subsidiaries, 5 associate companies, 27 joint ventures, and 35 joint operations. As of 1 October 2023, S N Subrahmanyan serves as the chairman and managing director of L&T, having succeeded A M Naik.
